title: Nasdaq Falls 1.6% as Chip Rout Deepens and Iran Tensions Rattle Global Markets

body:
Key Takeaways
  • Nasdaq fell 1.62%, dragged down by a semiconductor selloff and geopolitical tensions.
  • Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is 23.5% below its June record, indicating a bear market.
  • Taiwan Semiconductor reported a 77% profit jump but saw its shares decline.
  • Brent crude oil surged 2.45% amid escalating U.S.-Iran conflict.
  • Japanese and Taiwanese markets dropped significantly, reflecting global market downturn.

U.S. stock markets extended their losses on Friday as a punishing semiconductor selloff entered its third consecutive day, dragging the Nasdaq Composite down 1.62% while escalating tensions between the United States and Iran rattled global risk appetite.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 418.14 points to 25,463.81, while the S&P 500 dropped 0.85% to 7,469.70 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.19% to 52,452.04. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has now fallen 23.5% below its June 22 record closing high, firmly in bear-market territory.

Chip Stocks Lead the Rout

The selloff was driven by heavyweight chip stocks despite solid corporate earnings. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. posted a 77% jump in quarterly profit and raised its capital expenditure forecast, yet its U.S.-listed shares still declined. Memory-chip makers including SanDisk, Western Digital, Seagate Technology, and Intel were among the largest percentage losers.

"This extreme volatility is very disconcerting for the average investor when they see these huge swings in their portfolio value," said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder. The semiconductor sector now accounts for over 20% of the S&P 500's weight, amplifying each chip-stock swing across broader indexes.

Geopolitical Turbulence Adds Pressure

The U.S.-Iran conflict escalated further on Friday, with American forces striking bridges and an airport in Iran while Tehran responded by hitting infrastructure in Kuwait. Brent crude surged 2.45% to $86.29 per barrel, while WTI rose 2.47% to $80.90.

Global markets followed Wall Street lower. Japan's Nikkei tumbled 4%, putting it 12% below its recent peak, while Taiwan's stock market plunged more than 6% for its worst day since April 2025. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares fell 2.7%.

What NRI Investors Should Watch

For Non-Resident Indian investors with significant U.S. equity exposure, the selloff presents both risks and potential opportunities. Indian IT stocks — whose fortunes are closely tied to U.S. technology spending — could face headwinds if the chip-led correction spills into broader tech budgets. However, Indian government bonds gained on the week as softer U.S. inflation data eased concerns about an immediate Fed rate hike.

Treasury yields fell on the day, with the 10-year note at 4.525% and the 2-year at 4.137%, as markets priced out a July rate hike. Gold touched $3,999.49 an ounce. The defensive rotation — into bonds, utilities, and energy stocks — suggests investors are bracing for a volatile stretch heading into next week's tech earnings from Alphabet, Tesla, Intel, and Texas Instruments.
